# FableCut

> A Premiere-style video editor that runs in the browser and keeps its entire
> timeline in one JSON file, so an AI agent can edit video through MCP or a
> REST API while a human watches the cut change. MIT licensed, zero npm
> dependencies, runs locally on your own machine.

FableCut is not a cloud service and has no black-box render API. The whole edit lives in `project.json`. An
agent rewrites that file the way it rewrites code; the open editor reloads in
about 150 ms. A human and an agent can work the same timeline at once.

## Facts

- License: MIT. Free for personal and commercial use. No account, no telemetry,
  no paid tier.
- Requirements: Node.js 18+ and a Chromium-based browser. ffmpeg on PATH is
  optional but recommended (fast export, upload remuxing, loudness
  normalization, auto-duck and noise reduction).
- Install: `npx -y fablecut`, then open http://localhost:7777 (projects and
  media go to ~/FableCut). Or clone the repo and run `node server.js`.
- MCP: `claude mcp add -s user fablecut -- npx -y fablecut mcp` (any client:
  command `npx`, args `-y fablecut mcp`).
- No install: FableCut Studio (https://studio.fablecut.space) runs the same
  editor in a Chromium browser on a folder on the user's disk; clips are never
  uploaded; an agent's edit commands and the frames it asks to see pass through a relay. Agents connect by link (Claude Code, claude.ai, ChatGPT or any MCP
  client). Docs: https://fablecut.space/docs/studio/
- The server binds 127.0.0.1 only. Media stays in a local folder; nothing is
  uploaded to a cloud service.
- Control surfaces: an MCP server (stdio, client-neutral), a REST API, and
  direct edits to `project.json` with live reload over server-sent events.
- Editing: multi-track video and audio (up to 16 per kind), per-clip volume,
  stereo pan, speed ramps, keyframes, transitions, titles with kinetic text
  animation, SVG library, chroma key, AI background removal.
- Audio: a mixer with track faders, pan, mute / solo and meters; submix buses;
  clip gain; effect chains (EQ, filters, compressor, limiter, gate, delay,
  reverb, distortion, stereo width, pitch shift) with presets and keyframed
  parameters; loudness normalization (LUFS); auto-duck; crossfades; noise
  reduction.
- Color: a Color workspace with GPU grading per clip or adjustment layer
  (lift / gamma / gain / offset wheels, exposure, white balance with a picker,
  blacks / shadows / midtones / highlights / whites, log-style contrast and
  pivot, soft rolloff, saturation, luma / RGB curves and hue vs hue / sat /
  luma and sat vs luma curves, and layers — secondaries limited by an HSL
  qualifier and / or a keyframable ellipse, rect, polygon, bezier or free-hand
  mask) and live scopes (waveform, RGB parade,
  vectorscope, histogram). Agents grade with the `setGrade` patch op and read
  the result as numbers with `fablecut_scopes`.
- Masks: cut what any clip shows (video, image, SVG, text, adjustment layer)
  with rectangle, ellipse, bezier-pen and free-hand shapes, several per clip,
  combined with add / subtract / intersect / difference, with feather,
  expansion, invert and opacity, all keyframable. Agents use the `setMask`
  patch op and measure coverage with `fablecut_scopes`.
- Motion tracking: follow a point or region (optionally its scale and
  rotation) through a video clip; masks follow it and other clips pin to it
  as editable keyframes. Agents use the `fablecut_track` tool.
- Shapes, nulls and parenting: shape layers of rectangles, ellipses,
  polygons, stars, lines and bezier paths in nested groups, with fill, stroke,
  dashes and trim paths (draw-ons), every value keyframable; invisible null
  objects; parenting chains; an anchor point on every clip. Agents use the
  `setShape` and `setParent` patch ops.
- Motion paths, motion blur and text on a path: position keys with bezier
  handles bend a clip's travel (auto-orient turns it along the way); a
  shutter-angle motion blur samples sub-frames in preview and export; titles
  run along lines, arcs, circles and drawn paths with a keyframable offset.
  Agents use the `setMotionPath` and `setTextPath` patch ops.
- Media management: the Project bin shows each file's frame rate, codecs,
  audio channels and size (ffprobe), searches and filters by them, by tag,
  favorite, collection or usage, and finds every place a file is used.
  Missing files are flagged offline and relinked (found by name and size) or
  replaced. Agents use the `updateMedia`, `setCollection`, `removeCollection`,
  `relinkMedia` and `replaceMedia` patch ops.
- Proxies: light H.264 copies of heavy footage played while editing; export,
  scopes and frame grabs always use the originals. Agents use `fablecut_proxy`.
- Projects: one install keeps many projects (./project.json is the open one); a
  dashboard opens, creates from canvas presets or saved templates, duplicates,
  renames, tags, annotates, archives and deletes them. Agents use
  `fablecut_projects`.
- Compositions (nested sequences): a timeline of its own, placed as one clip
  that transforms, masks, grades and blends like a picture while its media
  plays and exports; nests 4 deep, opens on the timeline, precompose a
  selection. Agents use the `addComp`, `updateComp`, `inComp` and `precompose`
  patch ops.
- Animation presets and templates: 33 named entrances, exits, emphases and
  loops keyed relative to the clip, and templates (lower thirds, logo
  animations, social layouts at 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9) with text, colour and logo
  fields, each placed as its own comp and retimed by its hold point. Saved
  ones live in library/presets and library/templates. Agents use the
  `applyPreset`, `addTemplate`, `setTemplate`, `savePreset` and
  `saveTemplate` patch ops.
- Track mattes and blending: a clip can be cut by the picture on the track
  above (alpha, alpha inverted, luma, luma inverted; the matte track stops
  drawing), and laid over the clips below with 17 blend modes. Agents use the
  `setMatte` patch op and `props.blend`.
- Delivery presets: YouTube, YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, TikTok, X,
  LinkedIn, Master, Broadcast (ProRes), Web, Archive (FFV1) and Custom, with
  resolution / reframing, frame rate, codec (H.264, HEVC, AV1, VP9, ProRes,
  DNxHR, XDCAM, FFV1), hardware encoders, CRF / VBR / CBR, keyframe interval,
  pixel format, color, container, audio, file-name templates and metadata;
  saved presets, and warnings about upscaling, crops and platform limits.
- Batch export: one project → many files (master, YouTube, reel, square,
  preview), one render per frame rate and range (up to 8 outputs each), saved with the project; an export queue with
  progress, stop, retry and open. Agents: `fablecut_export {outputs}`.
- Delivery checks: loudness normalization (two-pass loudnorm, true-peak
  ceiling) and a report on every exported file — size, frame rate, frames,
  codecs, length, loudness, true peak and file size against what was asked.
- Export: fast ffmpeg export via delivery presets or encoding profiles, WebCodecs hardware export
  (browser encodes H.264, server muxes), and a realtime MediaRecorder fallback.
  Agents can start an export themselves (`fablecut_export`), in the open editor
  or a headless browser.
- Look at the footage: agents can fetch a JPEG of any frame (`GET /api/frame`),
  an N-up contact sheet across a clip, or the composed timeline as the
  compositor renders it — or text-only measurements of the same for models
  without vision (`fablecut_frame`, `text:true`).
- Also installable as a Claude Code plugin, which registers the MCP server and
  adds `edit-video`, `remake-reel` and `motion-graphics` skills.
